html:
Wat Xieng Thong is a Buddhist temple in Luang Prabang, built around 1560 by King Setthathirath where the Khan River meets the Mekong. Its sweeping roofs, low to the ground, are the classic Luang Prabang style.

Kings of Lan Xang and later of the Luang Phrabang kingdom were crowned here. Its walls carry a glass mosaic of the tree of life, and it houses the royal funeral carriage.

The temple survived the sack of the city by Chinese raiders in 1887. Luang Prabang, with dozens of temples and French colonial houses, was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995, and monks still walk its streets each morning to collect alms. See Theravada.
